newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut hopes US travel ban will be lifted.
newsitem.headline: Beirut hopes US travel ban will be lifted.

text.p: The United States will make a move towards lifting its 11-year-old travel ban on Lebanon at a Washington donors meeting next week, a Lebanese minister said on Wednesday.
The Friends of Lebanon meeting called by President Bill Clinton for December 16 will group countries interested in giving Lebanon financial assistance for national reconstruction.
"I think there is an American awareness of the unhelpfulness of this ban and there definitely will be some sort of initiative in that direction," Foreign Minister Fares Bouez told a news conference.

The ban on U.S. citizens travelling to Lebanon was imposed in 1985 after Moslem guerrillas hijacked a Trans World Airlines plane to Beirut during the 1975-90 Lebanese civil war and killed a U.S. citizen on board.
Bouez said it was not clear whether the United States would lift the ban or take a gradual step towards doing so.
The Friends of Lebanon conference was proposed in a U.S.-brokered understanding on April 26 that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon.
Lebanon hopes to get up to $5 billion for use over the next five years on reconstruction projects.
Bouez said the diversity of the projects would open many ways for countries to extend their support whether through soft loans, semi-soft loans, commercial loans or direct financing.
"This diversity will also open the way for countries to choose the subject which they see as most important for them whether in the environment, education, or health," he said.
